summary: Cap-de-la-Table (Table Head): an octagonal concrete tower of 1917-1918 on the north coast of Anticosti Island, automated in 1970; the site is controlled by an outfitter, per LighthouseFriends.

structures.note: Built 1917-1918; about 12 m (40 ft) from base to vane; white, with a red lantern.

access.note: Tower closed to visitors (Lighthouse Directory: 'Site open, tower closed'). LighthouseFriends says Safari-Anticosti Outfitters controls the site and advises checking with the outfitter before using the 39 km road.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (directory); site controlled by Safari-Anticosti Outfitters (LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Built 1917-1918 by the Department of Marine and Fisheries.
Fog alarm plant established; the 1917-18 report lists a fog alarm plant being erected at Table Head.
Light established in 1919 (LighthouseFriends; the Directory gives 1919).
Stations at Cap de Rabast, Charleton point and Table head, built during the war, in permanent operation by the 1920-21 report.
Oil storage tanks installed at Charleton point and Table head (fiscal year 1921-22 report).
New fog alarm building added; the fog alarm has since been discontinued.
Double dwelling demolished in 1959-60 and replaced by two separate residences.
Two keepers' residences demolished, after falling into disrepair.

corrections.why: The register and the 1989 heritage statement give the build as 1917-1918. 1919 is the year the light was established (LighthouseFriends, Directory).
The register (as reproduced by Heritage Guide) gives Recognized 1990, and LighthouseFriends also says 1990.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives 49.351184, -61.896157, which agrees with the record's OpenStreetMap point (49.3512, -61.8957). The Wikidata point (49.35, -61.88) is rounded to hundredths of a degree, about 1.1 km from the others, and is the outlier.
The record's 1919 is the year the light was established. The register and the heritage statement give the tower's build as 1917-1918.

notes_for_editor: Status is disputed and left open in the story: the Directory says Inactive; LighthouseFriends describes a lit light in 2012; the 2025 Coast Guard Atlantic list has no Cap-de-la-Table entry, though it lists Cap-de-Rabast. Recommend a current Notices to Mariners or Coast Guard check before the status field is changed; the record's 'active' comes from OpenStreetMap. Owner conflict: the 1989 statement and the Directory say Canadian Coast Guard; LighthouseFriends says the site is controlled by Safari-Anticosti Outfitters. Keepers: the four names come only from LighthouseFriends. I tried the Marine keepers' tables for 1914-1925; their OCR scrambles the columns and no Table Head keeper row was matched by position, so the names are unverified against the Department's tables. Check against page images before publishing. Range: LighthouseFriends says 'five miles'; the record uses 5 nautical miles; the unit is unverified. Marine reports print 'Charleton point' in 1917-18 to 1921-22; the story does not identify it with Pointe-Carleton. Record county is 'Minganie Regional County Municipality'; the Directory lists the light under Anticosti Island; check the county field. Keeper houses: the statement says 1959-60; the Directory says '(1960)'. Photos: none mirrored (LighthouseFriends photos are credited to Kraig Anderson; the Heritage Guide photo is credited to Transport Canada). Not used: Wikipedia and Wikidata (record only). Fact-check 2026-10-27: sessional numbers for the footnotes are read from the title pages (the 1921-22 title reads 'No. 28' in the OCR, so no number is given); the keeper accents are right in the raw bytes (é in Latin-1; the fetch text shows U+FFFD); the 2025 Coast Guard Anticosti section was searched in full for Table Head and la Table, with no entry found.
